newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares ended slightly weaker on Wednesday depressed by a soft bullion price. Industrial shares eased in sympathy and were further pressured by some profit-taking.
"Industrials have cooled off. They've had a good run in the last two weeks," a dealer said, adding, however, that underlying sentiment remained positive.
"If it pulls back much further we'll some support at lower levels," the dealer said.
Dealers said futures players had unwound baskets in the market, putting strain on share prices although this was minor as the stock had been absorbed.
Foreign and local players were seen taking profits.

Gold shares ended weaker but dealers said the market perceived bullion to be nearing its bottom. Bullion traded at a fresh 3 -3/4 year low on Wednesday falling below the $337 level. It fixed at $336.90 an ounce to record its lowest London fixing since April 13, 1993.
Traders said this had dragged the rand gold price to a year low.
The market was seen continuing taking a breather on Thursday and one dealer said it would end the week "flattish to firmer".
The overall index lost was down 8.3 points to 6,966.7 points, industrials lost 30.3 points to 8,262.8 points, and the gold index shed 8.3 points to 1,350.0 points.
RMB shares jumped on prospects of a surge in earnings in its subsidiary Momentum, dealers and analysts said on Wednesday.

Analysts said Momentum was expected to show earnings up a strong 40 to 50 percent in the year to June 30, 1997. RMB ended up 500 cents, or 6.1 percent stronger, at a fresh high of 85.50 rand. Momentum added a rand to finish at a record high of 49 rand.
Dave Southey, an analyst at Edey Rogers said that both RMB and Momentum appeared overpriced at current levels.
"I think its crazy. The shares are too expensive," he said.

De Beers and Anglo continued to attract interest. Dealers said it looked like the gem deal between De Beers and Russia might be signed soon. Interfax news agency reported on Tuesday that a deal was likely to be signed in February or March.
De Beers finished up 175 cents stronger at 150.75 rand, Anglo gained 200 cents to 270 rand, Freegold was up 85 cents to 33.60 rand but Kloof dropped 65 cents to 33.75 rand.

Near-dated industrial and all-share equity futures were weaker in later trade and dealers said the market was consolidating after good gains for most of last week. Gold contracts were softer on a weak bullion price.
The March all-share contract was last at 6,426/39 from 6,444, the industrial contract was at 8,012/25 from 8,055 and the gold contract was at 940/56 from 954.
